history.summary: Listed as a tourist place on the official Koderma district website (koderma.nic.in): a Radha Krishna temple 'in the midst of beautiful lake connected with a long pathway to enter the temple for prayer', 'situated in the centre of the city on the national highway', 3 km from Koderma Railway station and 4 km from the DC Office. No built date, founder, or architecture documented on that page. A SEPARATE, distinct shrine: Dainik Bhaskar (30 Apr 2026) reported a three-day pran pratishtha of Radha-Krishna idols at the Sankat Mochan Mandir premises, Jhumri Telaiya — not necessarily this lake temple; the two should not be conflated. Coordinates are Koderma town-centre approximation.

name: Radha Krishna Mandir
town_description: Koderma, often referred to as Jhumri Telaiya, is a town in Jharkhand and the headquarters of Koderma district. Once known as the mica capital of India, it lies along National Highway 31 between Patna and Ranchi.

travel.airport: Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Airport, Patna (~165 km)
travel.railway: Koderma Junction railway station (~3 km per district tourism site)
travel.road: Centre of the city on the national highway; 4 km from DC Office (koderma.nic.in)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Janmashtami is the main festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily; official hours not published - verify locally
